# Clause– Laws And Moods Silicons (such as cyborgs and AIs), thavens, and anyone unlucky enough to be on the receiving end of a cruel god's ire are bound to a set of guidelines called either "Laws" (for silicons) or "Moods" (for thavens).
In the case of Laws, these are all-binding– [bold]if a Law says you must do something, then you must do it[/bold], and vice versa for Laws stating you must not. Laws are prioritized in the order they are listed, from 1 (or 0 if applicable) onwards. If two Laws conflict, prioritize the one higher up on the list.
You may as a cyborg request to have your Laws reset, but you may not as the Station AI request for your Lawset to be modified. You also may not as the AI obstruct authorized personnel from entering your core or modifying your laws without having a law explicitly requesting it.
In the case of Moods, they should influence but not fully define how you play. Think of Moods as extremely strong impulses– you may ignore them at the cost of distressing yourself, or you may try to fulfil them to the best of your ability. If a Mood permits you to act in a way contrary to your job, characterization, or intent, you may disregard it, AHelp for a reroll, or attempt to follow through with it anyways.
In both cases, you may entirely disregard all roleplay expectations and exception clauses in how you act, as long as it is in the interest of fulfilling your Laws or Moods. [bold]You may not break server rules[/bold].
Absence of a relevant Law or Mood is not permission to act. You may not, for example, loose the engine because your Laws say you have to kill the captain. AHelp, or follow what you are given to the letter if unsure of what's acceptable.
